title: Vegas TCG Exchange
summary: From discovering an event to reserving a place at the table.
description: An event website for a Las Vegas trading-card community, bringing event information, vendor reservations, and registration into a focused web experience.
challenge: Give visitors practical event information while making the vendor reservation journey easy to follow.
approach: An event countdown, venue details, and expandable vendor guidance lead toward a Stripe payment link and a separate registration page.
features: Event information
Dates, venue directions, and a countdown bring key details together.
Vendor journey
A payment-link reservation flow leads vendors toward registration.
Expandable guidance
Accordion sections organize vendor rules and practical details.
next: Continue refining content, motion, and the steps a visitor needs to complete.

title: Inventory Management System
summary: Equipment, its status, and its next action in view.
description: A browser-based inventory interface organizing equipment records, assignment workflows, scanning, and reporting. Presented without organizational branding or operational records.
challenge: Move efficiently between finding an asset, understanding its status, and carrying out the next operation.
approach: Dashboard summaries connect to asset views and modal workflows. Orbital navigation provides another way to reach common actions.
features: Asset workflows
Dedicated interfaces handle asset details, assignment, unassignment, and check-in.
Scan and identify
Camera-based QR scanning, manual lookup, and printable QR labels connect the interface to physical equipment.
Reporting
Status and category breakdowns, recent updates, attention indicators, and JSON export support review.
Interaction design
Theme switching, role-dependent interface controls, and orbital navigation organize the experience.
next: Explore individually timed modal transitions and expandable content, with measured performance and accessible alternatives.

title: Project Eclipse
summary: A tactical world, built from interconnected systems.
description: An ongoing game project exploring procedural dungeons, directional combat, and expressive boss encounters. Development combines gameplay iteration, original encounter direction, and asset-performance work.
challenge: Bring complex encounters and animated characters into a playable world while keeping asset costs and frame-time spikes under control.
approach: Work proceeds in playable passes: test a dungeon or encounter, inspect behavior and performance, then refine the relevant system. Chorrona connects a spellcaster design to creature-driven attacks, directional damage, and front/rear animation views.
features: Procedural spaces
Room variations, multiple floors, stairs, and minimaps shape dungeon exploration.
Chorrona encounter
A mouth becomes a scythe, a scarf becomes a sword, and a doll participates in spellcasting. Animation communicates each ability.
Asset pipeline
The project is moving animations toward 30 stored keyframes per second with interpolation toward 60fps playback, preserving transparency and consistent sprite scale.
Performance iteration
Caching, selective asset loading, and measured playtests guide ongoing work on stutters and visual quality.
next: Continue refining attack animation quality and frame pacing. Performance optimization is ongoing; smooth playback is a target rather than a completed claim.

title: Gatoru Charging Animation
summary: A charging state turned into a small animated scene.
description: An animated phone-charging concept combining a floating character, a purple vortex, outward-moving ripples, and upward-flowing energy. The scene is developed as separate visual layers and assembled through successive animation passes.
challenge: Make the scene communicate energy being drawn upward while keeping its different motions aligned, readable, and consistent.
approach: Approve individual components before combining them. The vortex rotates slowly outside and accelerates inward; an enlarged core leaves room for a separate charge-percentage overlay. Ripples travel outward from the lower light source while energy moves toward the vortex.
features: Layered motion
Character movement, vortex activity, water-like waves, and energy paths are refined independently.
Motion direction
Inward spirals and outward ripples establish clear, complementary directions.
Frame alignment
Keyframes and interpolation are evaluated for smooth motion, alignment, and unwanted stretching.
Delivery formats
Transparent assets and animated previews support compositing and visual review.
next: Refine individual hair clumps and bandana-tail motion. Device integration and a live battery-percentage overlay remain separate from the animation prototype.

title: Project Zeal
summary: A home for the work, and the thinking that connects it.
description: A personal React website connecting software, infrastructure, community projects, and visual experimentation. The root site presents the wider Project Zeal collection.
challenge: Give different kinds of work enough context to stand on their own while keeping them part of one portfolio.
approach: The existing animated floating-island identity and theme switcher are paired with a gallery and dedicated case-study routes. Structured project data lets the collection grow.
features: Project pages
Each project has its own purpose, approach, capabilities, and next direction.
Visual identity
The site builds on its floating-island banner and light/dark theme.
Expandable stories
Native disclosure controls support pointer and keyboard interaction.
next: Expand the collection with further projects and original demonstrations as source material becomes available.
